title: Evaluating Neural Cartographic Relief Shading for Urban Environments: A Downtown Calgary Study Using High-Resolution DEM and DSM Data
abstract: arXiv:2608.20149v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: This article explores the performance of analytical and neural-based hillshading methods in a dense urban environment using high-resolution digital elevation model (DEM) and digital surface model (DSM) data for downtown Calgary. The study compares single-direction and multi-direction analytical hillshading with relief shading generated in Eduard, a machine-learning system originally developed to emulate Swiss-style shaded relief trained primarily on mountainous landscapes. Because Eduard was not designed for buildings, bridges, streets, trees, and other urban infrastructures, the central question is not whether it perfectly reproduces urban morphology, but whether parameter tuning can nevertheless produce visually strong, cartographically useful, and in some cases superior results when compared with conventional analytical methods. translated_title: 评估城市环境下的神经制图地形晕渲：一项基于高分辨率DEM和DSM数据的卡尔加里市中心研究
translated_abstract: 本文探讨了在密集城市环境中，使用高分辨率数字高程模型（DEM）和数字表面模型（DSM）数据对卡尔加里市中心进行解析式和基于神经网络的晕渲方法的性能。研究将单方向和多方向解析式晕渲与Eduard生成的晕渲进行了比较，Eduard是一个机器学习系统，最初开发用于模拟主要基于山地景观训练的瑞士风格晕渲。由于Eduard并非为建筑物、桥梁、街道、树木和其他城市基础设施而设计，核心问题不在于它是否能完美再现城市形态，而在于参数调整是否仍能产生视觉上强烈、制图上实用，并且在某些情况下优于传统解析方法的结果。分析特别关注地形类型、微观和宏观概括以及平坦区域细节参数。
tldr: 本文通过卡尔加里市中心的高分辨率DEM和DSM数据，评估了神经晕渲系统Eduard在城市环境中的适用性，发现通过参数调整可在城市制图中产生优于传统解析法的视觉和实用效果。
en_tdlr: This study evaluates the neural hillshading system Eduard in a dense urban setting using high-resolution DEM and DSM data from downtown Calgary, showing that parameter tuning can yield visually strong and cartographically useful results that sometimes surpass traditional analytical methods.
